families.Weave: The literal loom. Warp, weft, and the over-under rule that makes cloth out of thread.
families.Wave: A thread is also a signal. These are the shapes a running script makes.
families.Interference: Two simple things overlaid produce a third nobody specified. Automation's whole promise.
families.Orbit: Closed paths. Loops that return, knots that hold.
families.Order: The grid underneath. Packing, sequence, and the path the machine takes.

icons.title: Plain Weave
icons.note: The loom's atom. Three warp, three weft, strict parity — the only rule a plain weave has.
icons.doc: Parity interlace. Warp passes over weft where (i+j) is even.

icons.title: Shuttle
icons.eq: y = A sin(2π(x − x₀)/λ),  rails at the zeros
icons.note: A weft thread crossing four warp rails. Rails sit exactly on the zeros, so every meeting is a crossing.
icons.doc:
y = A sin(2pi(x-x0)/L). Rails sit on the zeros, so the ribbon meets each
one at a crossing and passes alternately over and under.

icons.title: Braid
icons.note: Three strands, 120° apart. Depth is the cosine of the same phase, so the plait resolves itself.
icons.doc:
Three strands, y_i = A sin(2pi x/L + 2pi i/3); depth z_i = cos(same).
Painter order is the sort of z, so the plait is exact rather than drawn.

icons.title: Twill Card
icons.note: A 2/2 twill draft — the diagonal of denim, and the binary matrix a Jacquard card punches. The first program was a fabric.
icons.doc:
A 2/2 twill draft — the binary matrix a Jacquard card punches.
Filled where (i+j) mod 4 < 2.

icons.title: Standing Wave
icons.note: Five phases of the same wave. The nodes never move — the fixed points a running script returns to.
icons.doc:
y = A sin(kx) cos(wt), sampled at five phases. Nodes are fixed; the
antinodes breathe between the envelope pair.

icons.title: Beat
icons.note: Two close frequencies summed. The envelope is emergent — nobody drew it.
icons.doc:
sin(2pi*3u) + sin(2pi*5u) = 2 cos(2 pi u) sin(8 pi u).
Two near frequencies; the envelope is the thing you didn't write.

icons.title: Packet
icons.note: One bounded event in an unbounded medium. The shape of a single run.
icons.doc:
A e^(-(x-c)^2 / 2s^2) cos(k(x-c)) — one bounded event in an unbounded
medium. The shape of a single run.

icons.title: Fourier
icons.note: Partial sums converging on a square wave, Gibbs ears and all. Small honest parts, one complex whole.
icons.doc:
S_N(u) = 4/pi * sum_{n odd <= N} sin(2 pi n u)/n. Four partial sums,
converging on a square wave. Composition, drawn.

icons.title: Moiré
icons.note: Two gratings crossed at 10°. Moiré is a textile word first — watered silk. The fringes are bigger than anything drawn.
icons.doc:
Two parallel gratings of pitch d1, d2. Beat pitch
L = d1 d2 / |d2 - d1| = 46*54/8 = 310 — four times either grating, and
nothing in the file is drawn at that size.

icons.title: Two Source
icons.eq: r = nλ from each of two sources 2a apart
icons.note: Circular wavefronts from two points. The hyperbolae between them mark where the two agree.
icons.doc:
Circular wavefronts r = n*lambda from two sources 2a apart. The
hyperbolae between them are where the two agree.

icons.title: Chladni
icons.note: The nodal set of a vibrating square plate. Sand collects on the lines that stay still.
icons.doc:
Nodal set of the (2,5) square-plate mode:
cos(2 pi x) cos(5 pi y) - cos(5 pi x) cos(2 pi y) = 0.
Where a vibrating plate stays still, sand collects.

icons.title: Lissajous
icons.note: A 3:2 ratio closes into a knot. Make the ratio irrational and it never returns.
icons.doc:
x = cos 3t, y = sin 2t. A 3:2 frequency ratio closes; anything
irrational never does.

icons.title: Harmonograph
icons.eq: x = Σ A e^(−dt) sin(ft + p)
icons.note: Four damped pendulums, detuned by 0.005. A Victorian drawing machine — automation before electricity.
icons.doc:
Two damped pendulums per axis:
x = sum A e^(-d t) sin(f t + p). Detuning f by 0.005 is what makes it
drift instead of repeat.

icons.title: Trefoil
icons.note: The simplest knot that cannot be undone. Every crossing is decided by z, not by hand. Drawn as plied yarn.
icons.doc:
(2,3) torus knot: x = sin t + 2 sin 2t, y = cos t - 2 cos 2t,
z = -sin 3t. z is exact, so every crossing is decided by the equation.

icons.title: Rosette
icons.note: A hypotrochoid — the spirograph. Three turns to close, with a second copy off by 30° for depth.
icons.doc:
Hypotrochoid, R=5 r=3 d=5:
x = 2 cos th + 5 cos(2 th/3), y = 2 sin th - 5 sin(2 th/3).

icons.title: Loop
icons.note: Lemniscate of Bernoulli. One curve, two lobes, one crossing — and the crossing is woven.
icons.doc:
Lemniscate of Bernoulli, x = a cos t/(1+sin^2 t), turned 45 degrees.
One curve, two lobes, one crossing — woven at the centre.

icons.title: Phyllotaxis
icons.note: The golden angle: the one divergence that never lets a row line up. 232 points, no collisions.
icons.doc:
Vogel's model: theta = n * 137.507 deg, r = c sqrt(n). The golden angle
is the only one that never lets a row line up.

icons.title: Serpentine
icons.note: As the ox ploughs. The shuttle's path across the warp, turning at each selvedge.
icons.doc:
Boustrophedon — the shuttle's path, turning at each selvedge.
Straight runs joined by semicircles of radius = half the row pitch.
